messages.author: b63e01cd28805f12
messages.subject: stat_density2d of ggplot2
parts:
Hello community,
I have the following problem with the function stat_density2d (2d density estimation.) the ggplot2 package


stat_density2d (mapping = NULL, data = NULL, geom = "density2d", position = "identity", na.rm = FALSE, contour = TRUE, n = 100, ...)


I require this function see the numerical calculation of the density estimate,

I have the following code and I can only see the graph, but not the values ​​of the density estimation (numerical values​​).

p <-ggplot (faithful, aes (x = eruptions, y = waiting))
p + stat_density2d (aes (fill = .. density ..), geom = "raster", contour = FALSE)

the above lines show the graphic, but I do not know, so that I can see
the numerical values ​​of the density estimation

In what way could see the numerical value of the estimate of density?


PD: The ggplot2 package says stat_density2d returned:

Value

A data frame

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: stat_density2d of ggplot2
parts:
Hi,

You can extract the values as using ggplot_build, like this:

p.data <- ggplot_build(p + stat_density2d (aes (fill = ..density..),
geom = "raster", contour = FALSE))[["data"]][[1]]

but note that in general if you need to use the results of a
statistical transformation outside of ggplot it is often easier to do
the transformation outside of ggplot. ?stat_density2d hints that the
transformation is done using the kde2d function (in the MASS package).
You may find it more convenient to use that function to compute the
densities.

BTW it also bothers me that the documentation for the stat_* functions
in ggplot2 state that they return a data.frame when calling them
returns a proto object, not a data.frame. I don't know why this is,
but I'd be curious to hear an explanation if anyone on the list has
insight into this.

Best,
Ista
